answers: Guess who's back? Serena Williams. And she made sure her return to the tennis court Tuesday was a stylish one, the Miami Herald notes, tweeting a picture of herself in a hot pink body suit. "Look who I spotted on the court. Her first day back," Williams wrote. She hadn't played since July thanks to health problems; click here to catch up on what's been going on. Her agent says Williams is "progressing well" and has the OK from doctors to do light cardio, but still has not set an exact date for her return to the WTA Tour.

full.prediction:
**Summary of News Passages**

In recent news, tennis star Serena Williams has made a significant return to training after a prolonged absence due to injury and illness. The 13-time Grand Slam champion, who had not played since July, posted a photo on Twitter showing herself serving in a hot pink full-length body suit, signaling her comeback. Williams, who had an emergency procedure for a pulmonary embolism in February, is still on blood thinners and has avoided long flights. Her agent, Jill Smoller, noted that Williams is progressing well and is engaging in light cardio, but no specific return date has been set. Williams is currently ranked No. 10 and has not withdrawn from the French Open, though her return to the WTA Tour is expected to be later, possibly at Wimbledon or the U.S. Open.

Meanwhile, world No. 2 Kim Clijsters also faced a setback, sustaining a severe ankle injury during a fall at her cousin’s wedding while wearing high heels. She is expected to miss the French Open and will require at least four to six weeks of recovery.

In a positive development, Ryan Sweeting, a 23-year-old from Fort Lauderdale, won his first ATP title at the U.S. Clay Court Championship in Houston. Entering as a wild card, Sweeting defeated Kei Nishikori in a hard-fought match. His victory boosted his ranking from No. 93 to No. 71, and he celebrated by jumping into the River Oakes Club pool, a tournament tradition.

The U.S. Fed Cup team will rely on young talents Christina McHale and Melanie Oudin in the upcoming world group playoff in Stuttgart, Germany. McHale, 18, and Oudin, 19, are set to replace Bethanie Mattek-Sands, who withdrew due to a hip injury. The German team, led by captain Barbara Rittner, acknowledges the potential threat posed by the young American players, who are eager to prove themselves on the international stage.
